title: State Medicaid Payment Policies for Medicare Cost Sharing (Policy in Brief)
note: As of May 2025, 41 states used lesser-of policies for physician services, 5 paid cost sharing in full and 5 used other policies.

title: 45 CFR 162.925: Additional requirements for health plans (HIPAA transactions)
note: If an entity asks a health plan to conduct a transaction as a standard transaction, the plan must do so.

title: 45 CFR 162.1602: Standards for health care electronic funds transfers and remittance advice transaction
note: Bank transfer format with the reassociation trace number that also appears on the electronic remittance.

title: Guidance letter GL-2022-04: health plans' payment of claims using virtual credit cards and the adopted standards for electronic funds transfer and remittance advice
note: Plans may pay by virtual card but must use the standard bank transfer and remittance when a provider asks, and may not require use of a vendor's services as a condition. Providers must ask their own bank to deliver the trace number.

title: Remittance Advice Remark Codes
note: MA18: claim forwarded to the supplemental insurer. MA19: not forwarded because the Medigap information was invalid. MA13: penalties for billing amounts not marked patient responsibility. MA130: unprocessable claim, no appeal rights.

title: Claim Status Codes
note: Used to check a vendor document's error code meanings: codes 4 and 5 concern requests for information, 21 is missing or invalid information.

title: Federal sequestration payment reductions
note: The 2% reduction applies to the final payment after deductible and coinsurance and is shown with reason code 253. Page dated July 7, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 149.620: Patient-provider dispute resolution process
note: A bill at least $400 above the good faith estimate is substantially in excess. The patient has 120 calendar days from the bill to start a dispute.

title: 45 CFR 149.510: Independent dispute resolution process (No Surprises Act)
note: Out-of-network commercial claims only. The arbitrator must not consider public payer rates, usual and customary charges or billed charges.

title: 45 CFR 160.103: Definitions (HIPAA), business associate
12 CFR 1026.2: Definitions and rules of construction (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z)
note: A creditor is a person who regularly extends consumer credit payable by written agreement in more than four installments, or subject to a finance charge. Regularly means more than 25 times in the prior year.

title: 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7k(d): Reporting and returning of overpayments
note: Covers funds received under Medicare or Medicaid. Deadline is 60 days after the overpayment is identified. An overpayment kept past the deadline is an obligation under the False Claims Act.

title: Florida Statutes 408.7057: Statewide provider and health plan claim dispute resolution program
note: Covers state-regulated insurers, HMOs and Medicaid prepaid plans. Excludes Medicare appeals, plans not regulated by the state and interest disputes. File within 12 months of the final determination.

title: Florida Statutes 409.908: Reimbursement of Medicaid providers
note: Subsection (13): Medicaid pays no part of Medicare deductibles and coinsurance when Medicare's payment equals or exceeds the Medicaid rate.

title: Florida Statutes 456.0625: Patient overpayments; refunds
note: Refund within 30 days after determining that the patient overpaid. A violation is grounds for discipline. Added by chapter 2025-48.

title: Florida Statutes 559.72: Prohibited practices generally (Florida Consumer Collection Practices Act)
note: Applies to any person collecting consumer debts, including an original creditor.

title: Florida Statutes 717.102: Property presumed abandoned; general rule
note: Dormancy period is 5 years unless another period is specified.

title: Florida Statutes 717.117: Holder due diligence and report of abandoned property
note: Written notice to the owner 90 to 180 days before reporting for property of $50 or more. Report before May 1 each year.

title: Revenue Cycle Management and Revenue Calculations (presentation to an HFMA chapter, November 2021)
note: Hospital scorecard targets: clean claim rate 85% or more, billed receivables over 90 days 20% or less, net denial write-offs 1.5% or less of net revenue, bad debt 2% or less of gross revenue. Based on PwC, HFMA, MGMA and HARA data. Not practice data.

title: Not-so-graceful aging: half of practices saw days in A/R increase in 2021 (MGMA Stat)
note: Quotes the 2021 MGMA DataDive Cost and Revenue median for receivables over 120 days in multispecialty practices: 13.54%.

title: What internal controls actually catch embezzlement in physician practices
note: The person who collects payments should not also post adjustments and reconcile the bank account. Article dated April 26, 2026. Only the public part was read.

title: Ask the Experts: Timely filing measurement
note: No industry standard known. One hospital respondent put timely filing at probably less than 1% of denial dollars.

title: Rate of initial denials of medical insurance claims continued to rise in 2024, Kodiak Solutions' proprietary data show (press release, syndicated copy)
note: Vendor data from more than 2,100 hospitals and 300,000 physicians. Providers collected 34.46% of amounts owed by insured patients in 2024, down from 37.58% in 2023.

title: Hospitals lost over $48B from claims denials, uncollected bills (report on Kodiak Solutions data)
note: Hospital medians: final denial rate 2.5% (2024) and 2.7% (2025), bad debt 1.1% and 1.3%. Overturn rate 42.1% in 2025. Secondary report of a vendor dataset.

title: Claims Denials and Appeals in ACA Marketplace Plans in 2024
note: 19% of in-network claims denied. Fewer than 1% of denied claims were appealed, and insurers upheld 66% of appeals.

title: 2026 UnitedHealthcare Care Provider Administrative Guide
note: One large insurer's manual, used as an example: rejected claims are not proof of timely filing, at least 90 days to file for participating commercial providers, disputes within 12 months of the remittance, virtual card payment when bank transfer is not set up.

title: A clean claim isn't a fully paid claim (2026 healthcare payments report card)
note: Vendor marketing based on 630 million professional claims: underpayments on 4.9% of claims, averaging 27% below the allowed amount. Method not published.

title: Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 30: Financial Liability Protections
note: Advance Beneficiary Notice rules. The notice is for Original Medicare and is not used for Medicare Advantage.

title: 45 CFR 149.610: Good faith estimates for uninsured or self-pay individuals
42 CFR 424.502: Definitions (Medicare enrollment)
note: Authorized official, delegated official (an owner or W-2 managing employee), managing employee, and owner (5 percent or more direct or indirect ownership).

title: 42 CFR 483.10: Resident rights
note: Paragraph (d): the resident has the right to choose his or her attending physician. The facility may seek alternate physician participation if the chosen physician does not meet requirements.

title: 45 CFR 164.308: Administrative safeguards (HIPAA Security Rule)
note: Paragraph (a)(7): contingency plan with data backup, disaster recovery and emergency mode operation plans (required) and periodic testing and revision (addressable). Unchanged as of November 6, 2026.

title: 26 CFR 1.1361-1: S corporation defined
note: Paragraph (l): one class of stock means all outstanding shares confer identical rights to distribution and liquidation proceeds under the governing provisions. Buy-sell agreements are generally disregarded.

title: HIPAA Security Rule To Strengthen the Cybersecurity of Electronic Protected Health Information (proposed rule, 90 FR 898)
note: Proposed 45 CFR 164.308(a)(13)(ii)(F): review and test contingency plans at least once every 12 months. A proposal only: not final as of November 2026.

title: Florida Statutes chapter 621: Professional service corporations and limited liability companies (sections 621.03, 621.09, 621.10, 621.11)
note: Shares may be issued or transferred only to licensed professionals or their professional entities. A disqualified owner must sever employment and financial interests forthwith.

title: File Annual Report
publisher: Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations
note: Annual report due by May 1. An entity that has not filed by the third Friday of September is administratively dissolved.

title: Practice Information: Corporate Practice of Medicine
note: Lists decisions a licensed physician must retain (including coding and billing procedures and payer contract parameters) and prohibited structures such as a medical practice run as a limited liability company.

title: Issue brief: Corporate Investors
note: States that the corporate practice of medicine doctrine varies widely by state and lists governance points for physicians dealing with corporate investors.

title: S corporation compensation and medical insurance issues
note: S corporations must pay reasonable compensation to shareholder-employees before non-wage distributions. The IRS may reclassify distributions as wages.

title: S corporations
note: Eligibility: domestic corporation, allowable shareholders only, no more than 100 shareholders, one class of stock. Election on Form 2553.

title: Beneficial Ownership Information Reporting
note: Final rule issued August 11, 2026 and effective August 14, 2026: US companies are exempt from beneficial ownership reporting.

title: Stay legally compliant
note: Corporations should hold annual meetings, record minutes, maintain bylaws and record stock transfers. Most states require an annual report or biennial statement. The address now redirects to the Manage your business guide.

title: Prepare for emergencies
note: Assess risk, create a plan, practice the plan with staff. A continuity plan should identify and document critical business functions. The address now redirects to the Manage your business guide.

title: Write your business plan
note: Traditional and lean plan formats. A lean plan is typically one page and can take as little as an hour. The address now redirects to the Plan your business guide.

title: Industry Segment-Specific Compliance Program Guidance for Skilled Nursing Facilities and Nursing Facilities
note: Physician arrangements such as medical directorships must reflect a real need, services actually provided, fair market value pay unrelated to referrals, and contemporaneous records such as time logs.

title: OIG Compliance Program for Individual and Small Group Physician Practices (65 FR 59434)
note: Physicians remain responsible for claims sent in their name by a billing service. Audits at least once a year: five or more records per federal payer or five to ten per physician. Medicare payments go to an account the provider controls.

title: AI Risk Management Framework: AI RMF Core
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
note: Voluntary framework. Govern function: inventory AI systems, document roles and responsibilities, define human oversight, leadership takes responsibility for AI risk decisions.

title: What is the difference between a compilation, review, and audit?
note: Compilation: no assurance. Review: limited assurance from inquiry and analytical procedures. Audit: the most assurance, with verification and substantiation.

title: Medical office embezzlement risk heightens at beginning of year
note: Reports an MGMA survey released November 5, 2010: nearly 83% of 688 practice managers had been affiliated with a practice where employee theft occurred. Describes concealment through write-offs and refunds.

title: Health leaders report they have 12-month strategic plans (MGMA Stat)
note: Poll of October 31, 2017, 1,212 applicable responses: 61% had a 12-month strategic plan, 34% did not, 4% unsure. Open poll, not a random sample.

title: Strategic plans can help guide medical groups in the short and long term (MGMA Stat)
note: 58% had a 12-month strategic plan, 37% did not, 5% unsure. Those with plans cite monthly financial statement review and quarterly progress checks.

title: The future of your medical group depends on who's ready when it matters most (MGMA Stat)
note: Poll of February 17, 2026, 302 applicable responses: 33% of medical groups have a succession plan for leadership positions, 60% do not, 8% unsure. 36% in July 2024.

title: Only 19% of practice leaders are very confident they could recover quickly from a cyberattack (MGMA Stat)
note: Poll of October 6, 2026, 238 applicable responses: 19% very confident, 61% somewhat, 21% not confident. Recommends a tabletop exercise twice a year. Notes 82% had a downtime plan in a July 2021 poll.

title: Survey: IT expenses per physician continue to rise to nearly $19,000
note: The most recent public MGMA figure found: $14,000 to $19,000 of technology operating expense per full-time physician in 2016.

title: Updated Special Advisory Bulletin on the Effect of Exclusion from Participation in Federal Health Care Programs
note: Issued May 8, 2013. No statute or regulation sets a screening frequency. The exclusion list is updated monthly, so screening employees and contractors each month best limits overpayment and penalty liability. Names billing and coding contractors and staffing agencies.

title: Health Care Fraud Self-Disclosure Protocol (updated October 15, 2026)
note: Not available for matters that involve only overpayments or errors, which go to the payer's voluntary refund process. Self-referral-only matters go to the CMS protocol. General practice: at least 1.5 times single damages. Minimum settlements of $20,000, or $100,000 for kickback matters. Samples of at least 100 items. Investigation findings due 90 days after the initial submission.

title: Health Care Fraud Self-Disclosure Protocol (web page with frequently asked questions)
note: Explains the four disclosure channels available in 2026 and states that items and services provided by unlicensed individuals are not payable by federal health care programs.

title: Justice Department's Civil Division and the Department of Health & Human Services Announce Anti-Fraud Healthcare Self-Disclosure Pilot Program
note: Press release of October 22, 2026. Six-month pilot for self-disclosing potential False Claims Act violations. Repayment with a 1.25 to 1.6 multiplier. Submissions accepted through April 22, 2027.

title: Corporate Integrity Agreement FAQ
note: Older agreements used a discovery sample of 50 paid claims, with a full sample and systems review if the net financial error rate reached 5 percent. Recent agreements review 100 claims with no threshold and require repayment of every overpayment found. Error rate is net overpayment divided by total dollars in the sample. Undated page, read November 10, 2026.

title: Targeted Probe and Educate
note: Contractors use data analysis to pick providers with high error rates or unusual billing, and services with high national error rates. Generally 20 to 40 claims a round, up to 3 rounds, then referral to CMS for possible 100 percent prepay review, extrapolation or referral to a recovery auditor. A low-volume version reviews fewer than 20 claims a round. Page last modified March 4, 2026.

title: Additional Documentation Request
note: Requests go to the practice address on file with Medicare, so the medical review correspondence address must be kept current. Best practice is to put the request letter on top of the response. Lists who reviews: Medicare Administrative Contractors, the Supplemental Medical Review Contractor, Recovery Audit Contractors and Unified Program Integrity Contractors. Page last modified March 4, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 405.903, 405.929 and 405.930: Prepayment review, post-payment review and failure to respond to an additional documentation request
note: 45 calendar days to answer a Medicare contractor and 30 to answer a Unified Program Integrity Contractor, with later acceptance for good cause. If the provider does not answer in time the contractor may deny the claim. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Medicare Fee-for-Service Compliance Programs
note: Describes medical review, recovery auditing and the Comparative Billing Report, which compares a provider's billing with peers in the state and nation. On November 2, 2026 the page said the reports were in development with release expected in late 2026 or early 2027.

title: CBR Guide - Part B
note: The Florida Medicare contractor's provider-specific comparative billing report is requested through its portal, and evaluation and management distribution reports are available on request. Peer comparison assumes each provider's specialty is reported accurately. Dated February 18, 2026.

title: Coding Trends of Medicare Evaluation and Management Services (OEI-04-10-00180)
note: From 2010 claims, flagged 1,669 physicians whose average visit level was in the top 1 percent of their specialty and who billed the two highest codes in a visit type at least 95 percent of the time.

title: Enforcement action: settlement of $41,739.66 for employing an excluded individual (Florida, January 6, 2025)
note: A solo practitioner settled after an excluded receptionist provided items or services that were billed to federal health care programs.

title: 42 CFR 411.353: Prohibition on certain referrals by physicians and limitations on billing
note: No Medicare payment for a designated health service furnished under a prohibited referral, and amounts collected must be refunded. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 411.354: Financial relationship, compensation, and ownership or investment interest
note: Paragraph (e): a required writing may be a collection of documents, and a missing writing or signature can be obtained within 90 consecutive calendar days if the arrangement otherwise meets an exception. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: CPI-U Updates: annual limits for physician self-referral exceptions
note: For calendar year 2026 the nonmonetary compensation limit is $535 and the limit on limited remuneration to a physician is $6,237. Both are adjusted each calendar year. Page last modified February 19, 2026.

title: 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b: Criminal penalties for acts involving Federal health care programs (Anti-Kickback Statute)
note: Subsection (b): knowingly and willfully paying or receiving any remuneration, in cash or in kind, to induce or reward referrals of federal program business is a felony. Bona fide employees are excepted. Subsection (g): a claim resulting from a violation is a false claim. Subsection (h): actual knowledge of the statute is not required.

title: Florida Statutes 456.054: Kickbacks prohibited
note: Unlawful for any health care provider to offer, pay, solicit or receive a kickback for referring or soliciting patients. Not limited to government payers.

title: Florida Statutes 817.505: Patient brokering prohibited
note: Unlawful for any person to pay or receive any commission, bonus, rebate, kickback or bribe to induce patient referrals to or from a health care provider or facility.

title: 45 CFR 164.404 to 164.410: Breach notification to individuals, the media and the Secretary, and by a business associate
note: Notify individuals without unreasonable delay and within 60 calendar days of discovery. A breach known to a workforce member or agent is treated as known to the practice. Breaches of 500 or more: notify the Secretary at the same time and the media. Smaller breaches: log and report within 60 days after year end. Business associates must notify within 60 days. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.524: Access of individuals to protected health information
note: Act on a request within 30 days. One extension of up to 30 days with a written statement of the reason. Fees limited to copying labor, supplies, postage and an agreed summary. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.520: Notice of privacy practices for protected health information
note: A provider with a direct treatment relationship gives the notice no later than the first service, makes a good faith effort to get written acknowledgment, and posts it only if it has a physical service delivery site. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.530: Administrative requirements (privacy training and documentation)
note: Train each new workforce member within a reasonable time and anyone affected by a material policy change, and document the training. No annual interval is stated. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.504 and 164.314: Business associate contracts
note: Required contract terms: report unauthorized uses, security incidents and breaches, bind subcontractors to the same terms, support patient access, return or destroy data at termination where feasible, and allow termination for a material violation. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.312: Technical safeguards (HIPAA Security Rule)
note: Unique user identification is required. Audit controls are a standard. Automatic logoff and encryption are addressable. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 414.1375: Promoting Interoperability performance category (Merit-based Incentive Payment System)
note: To score in this category a clinician must report completing the Security Risk Analysis measure during the year in which the performance period occurs. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Unified Agenda entry, RIN 0945-AA22: HIPAA Security Rule to Strengthen the Cybersecurity of Electronic Protected Health Information
publisher: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs
note: The 2026 agenda lists the rule under Long-Term Actions. The only completed step is the proposed rule of January 6, 2025. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Security Risk Assessment Tool
publisher: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT
note: Free downloadable tool (version 3.7) built with the HHS Office for Civil Rights for small and medium providers. Using it is neither required by nor a guarantee of compliance.

title: Florida Statutes 501.171: Security of confidential personal information
note: Notice to affected individuals no later than 30 days after determining a breach. Notice to the Department of Legal Affairs when 500 or more people in Florida are affected. A third-party agent must notify the covered entity within 10 days.

title: 42 CFR 1001.1901: Scope and effect of exclusion
note: No federal health care program payment for any item or service furnished by an excluded individual or entity, or at the direction or on the prescription of an excluded physician. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 1003.200: Basis for civil money penalties, assessments, and exclusions
note: Penalties may be imposed for arranging or contracting with a person the provider knows or should know is excluded, for knowing of an overpayment and not returning it, and for making a false record material to a claim. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 21 CFR 1301.13: Application for registration, time for application and expiration date (Drug Enforcement Administration)
note: Practitioner registration runs 3 years. Renewal may be filed no more than 60 days before expiration, and the agency emails a notice about 60 days ahead. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 410.75: Nurse practitioners' services
note: Medicare covers the services when the nurse practitioner works in collaboration with a physician as state law defines it, or under documented arrangements where state law is silent. The physician need not be present. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Florida Statutes 464.012: Licensure of advanced practice registered nurses; protocols
note: An advanced practice registered nurse works within an established protocol kept on site where the nurse practices, unless registered for autonomous practice under section 464.0123.

title: Florida Statutes 458.348 and 459.025: Formal supervisory relationships, standing orders, and established protocols; notice
note: A physician or osteopathic physician who enters a protocol with an advanced practice registered nurse must notify the board within 30 days, and again within 30 days of ending it. Both sections were read.

title: Florida Statutes 458.319, 459.008 and 464.013: Renewal of license
note: Medical, osteopathic and nursing licenses renew every two years. All three sections were read.

title: 42 CFR 493.37: Requirements for a certificate of waiver (clinical laboratory)
note: A certificate of waiver is valid for no more than 2 years. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Form Instructions: Advance Beneficiary Notice of Non-coverage (ABN), Form CMS-R-131
note: Deliver before the service with time to decide. The identification number field is optional and Medicare numbers and Social Security numbers should not appear on the notice. The patient must choose one option. The provider cannot bill a dual-eligible patient when the notice is delivered.

title: FFS ABN (Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage)
note: Issued to Original Medicare beneficiaries when payment is expected to be denied. Skilled nursing facilities use it for Part B services only. Page last modified July 17, 2026.

title: States with Telehealth Consent Requirements
note: Says most states have some telehealth-specific consent requirement in statute, rule or Medicaid policy, and that in Medicare the requirement is limited to communication technology-based service codes. Lists no reference for Florida. Entries updated through August 2026.

title: Florida Statutes 456.47: Use of telehealth to provide services
note: Telehealth services must be documented to the same standard as in-person services. The section contains no separate consent requirement.

title: 42 CFR 482.22: Condition of participation: Medical staff
note: The medical staff operates under bylaws, appraises its members periodically, and requires a history and physical no more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 482.24: Condition of participation: Medical record services
note: Entries must be dated, timed and authenticated. Orders must be authenticated promptly. Records must be completed within 30 days following discharge. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 483.45: Pharmacy services (long-term care facilities)
note: Monthly drug regimen review. The attending physician must document review of each reported irregularity and the action taken. As-needed psychotropic orders are limited to 14 days unless the prescriber documents a rationale, and as-needed antipsychotic orders cannot be renewed without evaluating the resident. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 483.75: Quality assurance and performance improvement (long-term care facilities)
note: The quality assessment and assurance committee includes the medical director or a designee and meets at least quarterly. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 424.20: Requirements for posthospital SNF care (certification and recertification)
note: Certification at admission or as soon after as practicable. First recertification by day 14, then at least every 30 days. Signed by a physician, or by a nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist or physician assistant with no direct or indirect employment relationship with the facility. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Florida Statutes 429.26: Appropriateness of placements; examinations of residents (assisted living)
note: Each resident must be examined by a physician, physician assistant or advanced practice registered nurse within 60 days before or 30 days after admission.

title: Florida Statutes 458.320 and 459.0085: Financial responsibility
note: Minimum professional liability coverage of $100,000 per claim and $300,000 aggregate, or $250,000 and $750,000 for physicians with hospital staff privileges, or an escrow account or letter of credit. A physician may go without under stated conditions and must then tell patients by sign or written statement. Both sections were read.

title: Is Your Insurance Keeping Pace with Your Practice? (Vital Signs)
note: Recommends regular insurance reviews and an annual conversation with an advisor as practices add staff, technology and risks. Written to promote the society's own insurance agency, so it is opinion, not data.

title: 29 CFR 2580.412-11: Amount of the fidelity bond for employee benefit plans
note: The bond must be at least 10 percent of the plan funds handled, with a minimum of $1,000, and need not exceed $500,000. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Florida Statutes 440.02: Definitions (workers' compensation)
note: Covered employment includes all private employments with four or more employees, or one or more in the construction industry.

title: 42 CFR 422.311: RADV audit dispute and appeal processes (Medicare Advantage)
note: CMS audits the diagnoses that plans submit for risk-adjusted payment and may extrapolate results for payment year 2018 and later. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 424.535: Revocation of enrollment in the Medicare program
note: Grounds include a pattern or practice of claims that fail Medicare requirements, failure to report changes or adverse actions on time, and failure to document or give access to documentation. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 405.378: Interest charges on overpayment and underpayments to providers, suppliers, and other entities
note: Interest accrues from the final determination for each full 30-day period that payment is delayed, and is waived if the overpayment is repaid within 30 days. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 411.355: General exceptions to the referral prohibition related to both ownership/investment and compensation (in-office ancillary services)
note: Paragraph (b): in-office ancillary services may be furnished personally by the referring physician, a member of the same group practice, or a supervised individual, so a solo physician can use the exception. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 411.352: Group practice (physician self-referral)
note: Paragraph (g): no group member is paid on the volume or value of his or her referrals. Paragraph (i): profit shares and productivity bonuses on personally performed work, including RVUs, are allowed. Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-06.

title: 29 CFR 1910.1030: Bloodborne pathogens
note: Written exposure control plan reviewed at least annually (paragraph (c)(1)). Training at initial assignment and at least annually (paragraph (g)(2)). Training records kept 3 years (paragraph (h)(2)). Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-06.

title: 29 CFR 778.211: Discretionary bonuses (overtime regular rate), read with 29 CFR 778.208
note: Bonuses promised in advance, including bonuses for quality and accuracy of work, production, attendance or staying employed, must be included in the regular rate used for overtime. Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-06.

title: 29 CFR 541.600: Amount of salary required (overtime exemption)
note: Exempt executive, administrative and professional employees must be paid on a salary basis at or above a federal weekly threshold ($684 a week in the text in effect November 6, 2026). The salary test does not apply to practicing physicians. Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-06.

title: Independent contractor (self-employed) or employee?
note: Common-law test in three groups: behavioral control, financial control and type of relationship. An employer with no reasonable basis for contractor treatment may be liable for employment taxes. Page last reviewed May 19, 2026.

title: Physician Demand Stabilizes Amid Rising Turnover for Recruitment Professionals, According to AAPPR Report
publisher: Association for Advancing Physician and Provider Recruitment, via PR Newswire
note: 2023 data from nearly 150 health organizations and more than 17,000 searches: median time from search launch to signed contract for physicians ranged from 77 to 228 days by specialty. The full report is paywalled.

title: Tseng, Kaplan, Richman, Shah, Schulman. Administrative costs associated with physician billing and insurance-related activities at an academic health care system. JAMA 319(7):691-697
note: Read as the PubMed abstract, PMID 29466590. Billing and insurance-related costs were 14.5% of professional revenue for primary care visits ($20.49 and 13 minutes a visit, including physician time), from 2016 to 2017 interviews at one academic system.

title: 45 CFR 149.420: Balance billing in cases of non-emergency services performed by nonparticipating providers at certain participating health care facilities
note: An out-of-network clinician at an in-network facility may not bill a commercially insured patient more than in-network cost sharing, unless the notice and consent rules are met.
